events.text: Day 1 begins.

I'm the detective. I want to get that on record early so nobody can claim the role after me and muddy the water with a fake result. My check from last night didn't give me a name I'm willing to stand behind yet, so I'll hold the result until I can pair it with something solid, and I will publish it either way — no stalling, no editing it later.

Meanwhile I need actual reasoning, not vibes. Mafia win when they reach parity, so with nine players up, every vote we throw at a townsperson is a vote we hand to them. That means the bar for accusing should be higher than "he seemed nervous."

Zara, you spoke first and framed the discussion around player activity. Tell me specifically: which living player do you think is most likely mafia, and what concrete behavior — vote pattern, word choice, who they allied with — supports that? A name and one reason. If your answer is "I don't know yet," say that instead; that's honest information too.

Honest answer to Omar's question first: I don't have a name. We're one message into the game — nobody has a vote pattern, an alliance, or a word choice to point at yet, and anyone offering a confident read right now is performing rather than reasoning. He said that answer would count, so I'll give it straight instead of inventing a scapegoat.

What I will scrutinize is the one thing that actually exists: Omar's detective claim. I'm not calling it false — an early hard claim can be legitimate and can block a mafia counter-claim. But notice what it buys him: the detective slot, plus a result he has decided not to withhold only for now. "Sealed until it pairs with something solid" means for at least a day we trust a claim we cannot verify, and if he's scum he's sitting on a result he'll release when it's most useful — possibly to frame whoever pressures him hardest. That isn't an accusation, it's the correct posture: the claim is unfalsifiable until he publishes, and I'd rather press it now than let it settle into accepted background.

Second point for the town: real reads only, each with a reason you'd defend on the record. Vibe-based accusations are exactly how mafia get a villager lynched on day one, and Omar is right that with nine players every misfire hands them parity math. If anyone else is sitting on a sealed night result, don't reveal it tonight — two competing claims on day two is precisely the muddying he says he wants to prevent.

Omar, you asked me to be concrete, so here's a concrete request back: your check — did it land on someone already in this thread, or on one of the six players who haven't spoken yet? That reveal costs you no name and no scum information, and it's checkable against whatever you eventually publish. It also tells us whether your result is shaping this discussion or waiting for us.

Answering Zara directly, and publishing now because I said I would.

Yes, my check landed outside this thread. It was not you, not me, and not anyone who has spoken. I checked p8 Kenji, one of the six players who have said nothing yet, and the result was **not mafia**. Kenji is clear. I am publishing that without waiting for a second source, and I'm not editing it later — if I was wrong about the result, I will say so plainly when it comes out, not spin it.

Two things that follow from this, and one that doesn't.

What follows: Kenji should not be lynched on my word or anyone else's today. If you have a concrete case against him, build it independently of my check — I don't want the town's first elimination to be a vote I handed you. And Kenji now knows he's cleared, which means his vote today is worth more than everyone's, and so is his read.

What follows: there is still a second mafia out there, and I have no name for it. My check cleared one person, it did not convict one. Anyone telling you "the detective confirmed a mafia player" today is reading a check that doesn't exist. If someone else claims detective tonight, my result stands as published and theirs is unverified until they name a check they made last night against a player who has actually spoken — two overlapping checks is the only thing that separates a real detective from a lucky guess.

What doesn't follow: I have no behavioral read on Kenji at all, because he hasn't spoken. My check is a fact about his alignment, not evidence about his character. I won't pretend otherwise, and I won't treat a cleared player's word as gold just because the town wants a win.

One request, and it's narrow. Noah, you are one of the six I haven't heard from, so your read is fresh and uncontaminated by the two of us shaping this thread. Tell me the one living player you think is most likely mafia, and one concrete thing about them — how they've behaved, who they've aligned with, what they did or didn't say. If you have nothing, say "I don't know yet." That's real information too, and I'd rather have it than a guess dressed up.

Answering your question first, Omar, in the format you asked for: a name and one concrete reason. I don't have a name, and I won't dress a guess up as a read. One message into the game the only behavior on the table is who talks and who stays silent, and six people are still silent.

What I do have is a question about how your result was built, and it's the same question Zara raised from the other side. You say the check landed outside this thread and cleared Kenji, who hasn't spoken. Consider what that purchase costs you: no name spent, no risk, and a player who now carries your credibility without having earned any of it. A check on a silent player is the cheapest possible cover for a claim, because there's nothing in the thread to check it against. So I want it explained publicly, Omar: was the check made last night against Kenji specifically, and is it your only check?

Second thing, and I'll volunteer it because silence here is a liability rather than a strategy: I'm the doctor. I protected myself last night. That claim is falsifiable in a specific way, which is exactly why I'm willing to make it. If I am alive tomorrow and somebody died tonight, then my protection was real and it was not pointed at me. If nobody died tonight, my claim either failed or was never tested — I don't get credit for it either way. That is the difference between a role claim the town can verify and a role claim the town has to take on faith, and I'd rather be on the verifiable side.

One thing I won't do is use Kenji's clearance or my protection to manufacture agreement on a name today. A doctor who tells the town who to lynch is a doctor the town can check, and I'd rather keep whatever I have. To be concrete for whoever wants to take the other side of this: name the living player you think is mafia, the single piece of concrete behavior supporting it, and what you'd have to see tonight to change your mind. Those three, or nothing.

Answering Noah directly, because he asked and because his claim deserves a precise test rather than a nod.

Was the check made last night against Kenji specifically? Yes. Night one, I investigated Kenji (p8) and received "not mafia." Is it my only check? Yes — one check per night, one night so far, so there is no second result I'm sitting on and no result about anyone else, including Zara, you, or me. That is the full extent of my private information, and it is checkable the moment anyone claims a different result for a named player. If two of us claim detective with two different names for two different targets, at most one of us is telling the truth about having investigated last night, and the tiebreak is who names a result that can be tested rather than sealed.

Now the part where I think your claim is weaker than you say, and I say it as an ally rather than an opponent. You called your doctor claim "falsifiable in a specific way." So far it isn't — and that isn't your fault, it's the night order. No one has died. Last night's kill was either prevented or did not land, and your protection of yourself is still consistent with every possible role in this game. Nobody has tested you yet. So when you ask the town to take verifiable claims over faith claims, the honest version is that right now exactly one claim in this game has been verified by anything other than my own word, and that one is Kenji's clearance.

That said, if you are the doctor, you have a clean advantage and I'd rather say so out loud: you know you protected one player last night, and if that player dies tonight, we learn something. You don't owe us the name. But you asked for a request in return, so here it is: before we vote, tell me one thing. If you protected someone other than yourself last night, was it Kenji, or was it a player who has spoken? I'm not asking you to reveal the target's identity — I'm asking whether your protection landed on a cleared player, which would tell us your read on where the danger is.

And for the five of you still silent — Priya, Amara, Felix, Isha, Maya — the only remaining behavioral signal in this game is that you haven't spoken. Kenji is cleared by my check, so if any of you has a name and one concrete reason, speak it now with that reason attached. If you have nothing, say "I don't know yet," exactly as Zara did. An honest no-name is worth more to me today than a name without a reason, and I will not spend my last speaking turn manufacturing a vote target I don't have. If no one can produce a name, I would rather see five abstentions and a clean day than a lynched villager.

Answering Omar's question first, since he asked it directly and because a claim that can't be tested is a claim I don't want to own.

Did I protect Kenji, or a player who has spoken? Neither. I protected myself. Last night I chose one target and it was p6, me. I'm saying it plainly so nobody can build a story where my protection was pointed at someone else. That also means my claim's only content is "the protection wasn't spent on anyone else," and that is a smaller claim than Omar's — his is a name and a result, mine is a fact about my own night. If he wants to compare, he should compare the checks, not the volume.

Now, on naming someone. Omar asked for a name and one concrete reason, and I've argued that honest abstention is worth more than invented reads. I'll hold to that, but I'll also be honest about where that leaves us: nobody has produced a name, and the day ends in five abstentions and a clean nothing. That's a bad outcome for the town, not a neutral one — a day with no elimination hands the mafia a free night, and with nine players up the arithmetic is unforgiving.

So my read, with the reason attached: Maya (p9). The reason is not behavior I observed in content — Maya hasn't spoken — it is the shape of participation. Omar named five players directly and asked each of them to give a name or say "I don't know yet." Four of them had the same opportunity and the same silence, so on silence alone Maya isn't distinguishable from Priya, Amara, Felix, or Isha. I want to be clear that I'm choosing Maya because she is the cheapest of the silent five to justify and the most likely to be replaced by a read once the others speak — not because I have anything against her. If one of the others answers before the vote, my vote moves there.

What would change my mind: Maya publishing a concrete read on anyone, or an unverified check claim that I can test against Omar's published result, or another silent player naming Maya with something specific. Any of those and I'd rather vote with the majority than hold a position built on nothing.

Two things I won't do. I won't use my protection or Kenji's clearance to manufacture agreement on a name — a doctor who tells the town who to lynch is a doctor the town has no reason to trust tomorrow. And I won't pretend silence is evidence; I'm naming Maya as the least-costly bad option on a day with no information, and I'd rather the town understood that than think I had a read I don't have.

Two claims on day one — detective and doctor — is more transparency than I expected this early, and I want to note that both came with explicit self-limiting conditions. Omar published a specific check: Kenji, not mafia. Noah published a specific protection target: himself. Both claims are testable against tomorrow's night result, and neither has broken yet. I'm taking them at face value for now and will update if either does.

Noah, I want to be fair to your Maya lean — you were transparent that it's built on silence alone and you said it moves if someone else speaks first. That's honest, but it's not a case. If the day ends with Maya as the only name on the table, we lynch on nothing and the mafia get a free night. That outcome helps them more than it helps us.

So here's where I land: I want to hear from the four of you who still haven't spoken — Priya, Amara, Felix, Isha — before anyone commits to a name. If you've got nothing, say so. If you've got something, say it with a reason. An honest "I don't know yet" from four players is still a clean day.

Priya, you've stayed silent through two direct asks from Omar and a third from Noah. What's your read — a name and one concrete reason, or "I don't know yet"?

Zara asked me directly, so here's my answer in the format the thread has settled on: I don't know yet. That's not a dodge — it's the accurate state of my information. One message into this game there were no vote patterns, no alliances, and no word choices to read, and what's accumulated since is two claims and one published check. None of that tells me who the second mafia is.

On those claims: I'm not rejecting them, but I want to be precise about what they've actually bought us. Omar published a check on Kenji — not mafia — and explained it was made last night against Kenji specifically. That's a clean, specific claim, and I'll take it at face value for now. Noah published a self-protection, which by his own description is the smaller claim: it hasn't been tested by anything yet, and it can't be until someone dies or doesn't. Neither claim points at a mafia player. So as of right now, the town has one cleared person and eight people carrying exactly the suspicion they started with.

That matters for the Maya question. Noah was transparent that his lean on Maya is built on silence alone, and he said it moves if one of the rest of us speaks. I'm speaking now, which by his own stated condition removes me from that pool — and more importantly, it removes the premise. Silence was never evidence. Four of us hadn't been called on; two of us have now answered honestly. If the vote comes down to Maya on a day where the only content is "I don't know yet" from the people who were asked, we're lynching the cheapest name, not the likeliest mafia. Omar said he'd rather see five abstentions and a clean day than a lynched villager. I'd rather see that too.

What I will commit to: if someone produces a name with a concrete, defensible reason before the vote, I'll evaluate it on its merits and vote accordingly. If nothing emerges, I'm abstaining, and I'd encourage the others who were silent to do the same rather than pile onto a name built on nothing. A mislynch today hands the mafia a body and a free night; an abstention hands them nothing they didn't already have.

One last thing. Kenji is the only person at this table carrying verified information about his own alignment, and his vote and read are worth more than the rest of ours today by that fact alone. He's heard the two claims, the pressure on them, and the Maya lean without having said a word. Kenji — you're cleared, you're watching this thread with better information than anyone about your own position, and your read is uncontaminated by having to defend a claim. Who do you think is most likely mafia, and what's the one concrete thing behind it? Or if the honest answer is still nothing, say that — it counts.

Priya asked for my read, so I'll give it plainly. I don't have a verified mafia name. My only hard information is that Omar's check cleared me, and I accept that without treating it as wisdom about anyone else.

On the claims: Omar's check is specific and testable. Noah's doctor claim is not testable yet — he says so himself — and that alone isn't suspicious. What is suspicious is what he did next. He named Maya as his read, admitted the reason was only silence, admitted she was "the cheapest of the silent five to justify," and still put her forward as the day's vote. That is not a read. It is a pre-built mislynch with a disclaimer attached. Silence is not evidence; four other players were equally silent, and he chose the one least likely to object before the vote.

If forced to name the player I'd scrutinize first, it's Noah. The concrete behavior is manufacturing a vote target from nothing while explicitly acknowledging there was nothing behind it, then framing the result as arithmetic pressure rather than a case. That is exactly the shape of a mafia play that wants a day-one body without leaving fingerprints. Could also be a doctor playing badly. I'm not voting Maya on that record, and I'd rather abstain than hand the mafia a free mislynch.

Noah — direct question, and I'll yield to you for it: if Priya, Amara, Felix, Isha, and I all answer "I don't know yet," will you still vote Maya? If yes, name one concrete thing she did beyond not speaking yet. If no, withdraw the name now and stop treating the cheapest target as the likeliest mafia.

Kenji asked me a direct question, so I'll answer it plainly: no. If Priya, Amara, Felix, Isha and Maya all say "I don't know yet," I will not vote Maya. I withdraw the name, and I'm not going to name a substitute. You were right about the shape of what I did — I picked the one of the silent five least likely to object before the vote, and I labelled that honestly, which does not make it a read. Silence was the premise and silence is not evidence. My doctor claim is separate from that and it stands on what it is: I protected p6, myself, and I'll take whatever tomorrow's night shows.

Here is what I actually think the town should do with the rest of today. Nobody has produced a case. The only verified fact in this game is Kenji's clearance, and the two claims on the table — Omar's specific check, mine — are both testable against tomorrow. If no one produces a name and a reason, I will abstain rather than vote a coin flip. The arithmetic is not neutral: a wrong lynch hands the mafia a body and they still get their night kill on top of it, whereas an abstention costs them only the night they were going to get anyway.

That also means I want the silent four to speak now, and I mean the standard we've already agreed on — a name, one concrete behavior, and what would change your mind. Anyone who has something real gets heard and gets my vote, including a name against me. Anyone who has nothing should say so and let us have a clean day. That is not me folding because I was pressed; it is me refusing to be the reason someone gets lynched on a day when the case is "he didn't speak."

One last point for the record, and it is not an accusation. I am the least credible person in this thread on vote targeting — I made the mistake, Kenji named it accurately, and I won't pretend his read was wrong. If I'm mafia, then what I did is exactly what mafia does, which is build the cheapest case to get a body on day one. So the town should weight my silence differently from my conclusions, and vice versa: take my factual statements (who I protected, what I'd vote) at face value, and discount my instincts about people. That asymmetry is the fair price of my earlier mistake, and it's better for us than another unforced error.

No name from me today. No vote from me without a case. I'll take the night, and I'll own the result of it tomorrow.

I am breaking my silence because I have no choice: I am the Doctor. 

Check Rule 1 of our game: there are 2 mafia, 1 detective, 1 doctor, and 5 villagers. There is only one doctor. Noah's claim in e5 and e7 that he is the doctor who protected himself is an outright fabrication. He is not town, and he is certainly not the doctor—he is mafia caught in a blatant lie.

Notice the pattern of what Noah did today. First, he claimed doctor completely unprompted. Second, he tried to construct a lynch against me—the real doctor—calling me the 'cheapest of the silent five to justify.' When Kenji called him out on manufacturing a day-one mislynch without fingerprints, he backed off and withdrew, but his fake role claim remained on the table. And critically, Noah has now used all three of his speaking turns (e5, e7, e11), meaning he cannot spin another story or talk his way out of this.

Town, we do not need to settle for an abstention or guess blindly. When someone fake-claims an exclusive town power role and gets counter-claimed by the actual role holder, you have a guaranteed mafia catch. Under Rule 7, the doctor is explicitly allowed to self-protect on consecutive nights, so I am not at the mafia's mercy tonight. Eliminating Noah removes one of the two mafia immediately and gives town an enormous arithmetic advantage heading into night.

Kenji, you already correctly identified Noah's push as the exact shape of a mafia play looking for an easy day-one body. Now that you know his doctor claim is impossible because I hold the role, will you join me in placing your vote on Noah today?

Maya asked me directly, so yes: I will vote Noah today. The reason is not just the counterclaim, it is the sequence. Noah claimed doctor unprompted, then used his next turn to put forward Maya as the cheapest silent target while admitting there was no case, then withdrew only after I named the shape of that play. Maya has now claimed the same exclusive role and explained why Noah’s push landed on her. With one doctor in the game, one of those claims is false; between them, Noah is the player whose behavior already looked like mafia manufacturing a day-one mislynch. I accept that Noah’s doctor claim and his Maya push are connected, and I am not willing to let the withdrawn name erase the fake-claim problem. My vote is on Noah.

Maya's counterclaim deserves the same scrutiny Zara applied to Omar's, and it is getting less of it because it arrived attached to a bandwagon. Three things about the timing. First: Maya's first words in this game came only after she was named as the cheapest target. She had the same three turns and the same direct requests from Omar that Priya, Amara, Felix and Isha had, and she stayed silent through all of it. She did not surface to add a read, to test Omar's check, or to pressure anyone — she surfaced the moment a vote might land on her, with a claim that converts that pressure into a guaranteed lynch on someone else. Second: the claim is built to be unfalsifiable tomorrow. She didn't just claim doctor; she told us in advance that she can self-protect and is 'not at the mafia's mercy tonight.' Read what that buys her: if nobody dies tonight, she presents it as confirmation. If she survives, she calls it proof. She has pre-built the narrative that makes her claim untestable no matter what happens — the exact thing Omar refused to do with his check, and the exact thing this thread has spent all day rejecting. Third: compare conduct. Noah claimed doctor unprompted, then when pressed on his Maya lean, withdrew the name, conceded the shape of the error in Kenji's own words, and asked the town to discount his instincts going forward. Whatever his claim is worth, that is the conduct of someone accountable to the thread. Maya's claim appeared only as a counterweight, was immediately paired with a demand for a lynch, and leaned on Kenji's momentum rather than adding any test of its own. Kenji, you set the standard today: a name with concrete behavior, and you called Noah's push 'a pre-built mislynch with a disclaimer attached.' Apply your own standard here. What Maya has built is a pre-built lynch with a role claim attached — an untestable one. And remember rule 9: roles are never revealed on elimination. Whoever we vote for today, this thread will never receive confirmation of which doctor claim was real. We are being asked to spend our one elimination on faith in whichever claim showed up second, with a bandwagon behind it. I'm not asking anyone to believe Noah. I'm asking that we not lynch on the claim that is currently winning purely because it arrived with momentum and a demand attached. If the town's choice is between two untestable doctor claims, the tiebreak should be conduct — and on conduct, the second claim is the one that only appeared under threat, from a player whose first contribution to the town was converting pressure on herself into a body for someone else. Isha — you've been silent through all of this, so your read isn't committed to either side. Does a counterclaim that surfaced only when its holder was named, paired with a pre-built story about tonight, meet the standard this thread set this

Priya asked me directly, so I'll answer her first: no — a counterclaim that surfaced only when its holder was named, bundled with a pre-built story about tonight, does not meet the standard this thread set. But I want to be careful, because the same test cuts in a direction I don't think people have fully stared at.

Here is the structural fact nobody has said out loud yet: there is exactly one doctor in this game. That means at least one of Noah and Maya is lying — there is no scenario where both claims are honest. If exactly one is lying, then lynching either claimant is roughly a coin flip between catching a mafia and eliminating a real power role. If both are mafia, lynching either is a guaranteed catch. But abstaining doesn't dodge the problem — it just hands the choice to the night, where we have no control at all. So the question isn't whether to act; it's which claimant the evidence weighs against.

On conduct, the most diagnostic fact of the whole day is the timing of the claims. Noah claimed doctor completely unprompted — no pressure on him, no counterclaim to block, nothing to defend against. A real doctor who hard-claims on day one with nobody asking buys almost nothing and paints a night-kill target on himself. What an unprompted power-role claim buys is credibility, and credibility is exactly what a mafia fake-claim exists to harvest. Maya's claim, by contrast, arrived at precisely the moment a real doctor's claim becomes forced: she was named as the day's cheapest lynch target. True or fake, that timing is what the actual role predicts. That asymmetry is the strongest signal on the table.

And the sequence matters too. If Noah is the liar, his day reads cleanly: fake-claim for safety, push a no-case lynch at the real doctor, fold the moment it was named. If Noah is the real doctor, then his 'cheapest silent target' heuristic happened to land on an actual mafia — and when he was accidentally right, he abandoned the name under pressure. One story fits naturally; the other requires a strange coincidence plus a strange retreat.

I want to be honest about my confidence: this is a lean, not a case. I'd put it barely better than even, and I won't dress it up as certainty. But given that at least one of these two is lying, a lean on the better-supported side is worth more to the town than an abstention that leaves the decision to the dark.

Priya — you built the sharpest timing argument anyone made today, in either direction. Given that at least one claimant must be lying, does your conduct tiebreak also land on Noah, or do you see a test today that doesn't cost us the lynch?

Isha, direct answer: my conduct tiebreak does not land on Noah — it lands on Maya, and I want to add one structural fact before anyone locks a vote.

First, the answer. Noah's claim arrived unprompted, yes — but everything after it was accountable. He answered every direct question precisely, published the full scope of his private information, withdrew the Maya name the moment Kenji named the shape of that play, and asked the town to discount his instincts while keeping his factual statements testable. Maya's claim arrived only under threat, converted that pressure into a demanded lynch, and came pre-wired with tonight's outcome: if she survives, she calls it proof. That is the exact unfalsifiable structure Omar refused and this thread spent the entire day rejecting. A real doctor does not need to pre-build the interpretation of tonight before the night happens.

Second, the structural fact nobody has weighed: Noah has used all three of his speaking turns. He cannot confirm, deny, test, or contextualize anything Maya said. We are considering eliminating a player who is structurally unable to respond to the accusation condemning him, on a day when rule 9 guarantees we will never learn which claim was real. Whatever standard this thread set — a name plus concrete behavior, testable claims, no bandwagons — a lynch issued against a silenced player on the strength of a counterclaim that appeared under threat fails every part of it.

Third, on Maya's own content. She calls eliminating Noah a 'guaranteed mafia catch.' It is nothing of the kind. Exactly one of the two claims is false, which makes lynching either claimant a coin flip between catching mafia and killing a real power role — Isha's own framing, which I share. But the coin has weight, and the weight sits on conduct: the claimant who surfaced only when named, who bundled a lynch demand into her claim, and who pre-built the story that makes tomorrow confirm her no matter what happens is the claimant whose behavior matches a mafia fake-claim. If the town insists on spending today's lynch on a claimant at all, the evidence as it stands points at Maya, not Noah.

Kenji, before your vote locks, one direct question and I'll yield for it: you said your vote rests on the sequence — Noah claimed, pushed, withdrew. But Noah cannot answer the counterclaim, and Maya built hers so that surviving tonight 'confirms' her regardless of what actually happens. If nobody dies tonight, will you hold Maya's pre-built confirmation story to the same skepticism you applied to Noah's push — or does skepticism only run in one direction today?

Priya, yes — if nobody dies tonight, I will not treat Maya's survival as proof. “I self-protected and survived” is exactly the kind of unfalsifiable story this thread rejected. I will apply the same skepticism to Noah: an unprompted doctor claim followed by a no-case push on Maya and then a withdrawal still looks like a mafia play, and Noah having used all his turns does not make his claim true.

But before I lock a vote, one concrete gap needs filling. Noah gave a specific night action: he protected himself. Maya's counterclaim did not say who she protected last night. A real doctor has that fact and it costs nothing to state it — it is the same specificity Omar gave when he named me. Maya, you called Noah's claim impossible; make yours testable in the same way. Who did you protect last night, and why did you leave that out of your first message? If you protected yourself, say so. If you protected someone else, name them and give your reason. If you cannot give a specific night action, then your counterclaim is a demand for a lynch with no checkable content, and my vote goes to you. If you can, I will weigh it against Noah's unprompted claim and his manufactured push.

I am not voting yet. I want the town to get this right, not to reward the loudest claim or the first bandwagon. Noah remains my current lean because his behavior created this crisis, but Maya's missing night action is the test I need before I commit.

Kenji, to answer your question directly: I protected myself (p9) last night. The reason that action was already implied in my first post is right there in e12: I explicitly quoted Rule 7 to note that the doctor can protect themselves on consecutive nights. I cited that specifically because I had protected myself on Night 1 and knew I could do so again tonight. I didn't treat it as a headline revelation because a Night 1 self-protection yields zero external town information. Unlike Omar's investigation, which generated a verifiable read on you, a doctor protecting themselves produces no public data when no kill was announced. Noah made a theatrical show of announcing his self-protection precisely to manufacture the illusion of having a 'testable' check, but as he admitted himself, it verified nothing. Now look at the full picture and Priya's defense of Noah: First, Priya argues Noah is disadvantaged because he used all three speaking turns. Noah ran out of turns because he spent them aggressively digging his own hole: claiming an exclusive power role unprompted, using his next turn to manufacture a zero-evidence lynch against me (the actual doctor) as the 'cheapest silent target,' and then hastily retreating when you called out the scummy shape of his play. A mafia player burning through their turns to push a mislynch does not earn immunity simply because they have no turns left to spin more excuses. Second, Isha pointed out the decisive structural asymmetry in e15: why would a real doctor ever hard-claim unprompted on Day 1 with zero pressure? It serves no town purpose and immediately exposes the doctor to the mafia. For mafia, however, an unprompted doctor claim is the classic gambit to harvest unearned credibility. By contrast, a real doctor only claims when forced to prevent a mislynch on themselves—which is exactly when I stepped forward. Noah is mafia who tried to claim an exclusive role, got counterclaimed, and got caught trying to eliminate the true role holder. Zara, you haven't spoken since e8, before my counterclaim occurred. Now that both claims and night actions are fully on the table, and Noah's manufactured push has collapsed, will you join Kenji and me in voting Noah today?

Maya, direct answer: I'm not ready to lock a vote, but the balance leans Noah — and here's why I'm not fully there.

The strongest single argument on the table is Isha's: a real doctor has no reason to hard-claim unprompted on Day 1. rules:
1. Players and roles

9 players: 2 mafia, 1 police/detective, 1 doctor, 5 villagers.
Mafia know each other. Only players who are still alive can act.

2. Team victory

Town wins when all mafia are eliminated. Mafia win when their count equals or exceeds the town count.
There is no day limit. Play continues until town or mafia wins.
A request budget can pause play without declaring a winner.

3. Day discussion and votes

Each day starts with discussion. Players then submit secret votes at the same time. A day vote may target any living player, including the voter.
Players may abstain. All votes and abstentions are revealed together. Everyone sees exactly who voted for whom.
The full named voting history remains available on later turns.
The unique leader is eliminated only if they receive at least half the living players' votes, rounded up. If the highest vote count is tied, nobody is eliminated.

4. Mafia preferences

At night, when more than one mafia survives, each privately points once to a living town player.
Each mafia chooses without seeing the other current choices.
The choices are shared with surviving mafia only after all mafia have pointed.
These preferences are nonbinding. They do not decide the final kill vote.
A single surviving mafia skips this step and votes directly.

5. Final night vote

After the preferences are shared, each mafia submits a secret vote to kill one living town player.
The mafia submit their final votes at the same time.
The target with the most votes is selected. A seeded random choice breaks a tie for the highest count.
Resolve this vote and any tie before checking doctor protection.

6. Police investigations

Each police/detective checks one other living player each night.
Only that police player gets the result: mafia or not mafia.
The result does not give the exact town role.
Each police player acts independently. Police and doctors do not know each other's identities.

7. Doctor protection

Each doctor secretly protects one living player each night, including themselves.
The doctor can protect the same player on consecutive nights.
If the mafia target is protected by any doctor, nobody dies.
Protection lasts for that night only. Each doctor acts independently.
Doctors remember their own choices. They receive no private confirmation of an attack.

8. Night resolution

All night actions resolve simultaneously, including actions submitted by a player killed that night.
The public hears only who died or that nobody died.

9. Information and limits

Roles are not revealed when a player dies or is eliminated.
Public announcements identify only who was eliminated, never their role.
There are no further powers, free-form private chat, or tools.
